A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HypRAG research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original MTEB and RAGBench evaluations, hierarchy probes, pooling and retrieval-context ablations, and a qualitative retrieval case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds MeSH retrieval, ANN, runtime, pooling-sensitivity, hubness and Qwen-based comparisons.

M1.justification: The architectures and OEM pooling operator are retained, but Section 4.4 revises the stated training objectives. Stage 2 gains the missing InfoNCE denominator; Stage 3 replaces the multi-positive supervised expression with a single-positive objective using in-batch and mined hard negatives. These are changes to the written specification; the PDFs do not establish that the original experiments were retrained.

E1.justification: v2 adds MeSH/PubMed hierarchy-sensitive retrieval, requiring discrimination between target abstracts and ancestor, sibling and unrelated distractors. It also extends the reported use of MS MARCO from embedding-curvature analysis to ANN and hubness retrieval experiments. Existing training corpora, MTEB coverage and the five RAGBench datasets remain.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Qwen-Embedding as a comparator alongside a Qwen-based HyTE-H instantiation. The pooling comparison expands from CLS versus OEM in v1 Table 4 to include Naive Pooling and Einstein Midpoint in v2 Table 7. Existing comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include 300 zero-shot MeSH queries at depths 3–6 with SpecHR, recall and MRR; ANN recall against exact neighbors on 100,000 MS MARCO passages and 6,980 queries; and latency for 32 queries on an H100. v2 also introduces an OEM exponent sweep and hubness measurement at k=10. The original MTEB and RAGBench protocols remain.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of the proposed mechanism: naive and Einstein pooling controls, sensitivity to the OEM exponent, MeSH errors separated by distractor type, and quantitative hubness analysis. These examine outward weighting, specificity errors and retrieval concentration beyond v1's CLS comparison and norm probe. The previous similarity-function and context-size ablations and Bixby case study are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised. The existing hierarchy figure is unchanged, and the new tables report point estimates. Hubness skewness is an evaluation metric, not a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Principal existing scores are retained, while substantial new results appear. MeSH Recall@1 is 0.963 for HyTE-FH versus 0.810 for EucBERT; newly evaluated Einstein and naive pooling obtain MTEB means of 50.33 and 47.07 versus OEM's retained 56.41. Additional results cover Qwen variants, ANN recall, exponent sensitivity and hubness. Runtime measurements report 22.48 ms for HyTE-FH versus 15.21 ms for EucBERT per 32 queries. These are added comparisons, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The original propositions, theorems and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. v2 adds an explicit Lorentz-to-MIPS sign-flip argument in Section 4.4 and defines SpecHR in Appendix E. The contrastive-loss equations are also substantively corrected or reformulated.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: two hyperbolic retrievers, hierarchy-preserving OEM pooling, up to 29% RAG gains, radial hierarchy encoding and parameter efficiency. New experiments support these existing claims. Removing the conclusion's speculative reference to future scalable and multimodal retrieval does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking OEM's radial spread to reduced hubness and more navigable HNSW graphs, interprets excessive outward weighting as amplifying outliers, and uses MeSH errors to argue for specificity discrimination. Appendix D newly acknowledges approximately 48% HyTE-FH latency overhead and attributes it to unoptimized hyperbolic kernels. These materially expand the mechanism and efficiency discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the 16,384 pretraining batch size, OEM default p=1, a hard-negative mining reference, FAISS indexing and sign-flip instructions, timing configurations, and the MeSH construction recipe. It also replaces the anonymous code-access pointer with a named GitHub repository. These substantially expand reproducibility information; newly disclosed defaults do not establish changes to earlier experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Oord et al. (2018) for InfoNCE and Nussbaum and Duderstadt (2025) for training and hard-negative mining, while removing Izacard et al. (2021). Appendix E additionally positions the diagnostic benchmark against a claimed gap in hierarchy-sensitive evaluation. The broader relationship to hyperbolic representation learning and existing RAG approaches is retained.

P1.justification: The training stages and ablation discussion receive localized rewrites, with new experimental subsections and a MeSH Appendix E that shifts Additional Results to Appendix F. Correspondence and publication-header text also change. Most introductory, architectural and theoretical prose remains intact, so this is not an extensive narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for ANN retrieval, MeSH scores and errors, empirical latency, exponent sensitivity and hubness. It expands the RAG comparison and pooling tables and redistributes existing tables across the revised layout. This substantially enlarges the visual presentation of evidence; Figures 1–4 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct empirical comparison with the Einstein midpoint and a retrieval diagnostic using known taxonomy levels. v2 supplies both, with sensitivity and hubness analyses that substantially strengthen evidence for its central pooling and hierarchy claims. Runtime measurements also expose practical costs. A material qualification is that the new HNSW explanation extends the query-document sign-flip identity to graph geometry without establishing that extension; this limits the secondary efficiency interpretation but does not outweigh the stronger central evaluation.
